history.period: Modern (rebuilt; earlier shrine ~100 years per oral tradition — verify)
history.summary: A modern temple on Kalibari Road, Chandwara, Muzaffarpur, built on the lines of the Katra Vaishno Devi shrine in Jammu & Kashmir, with idols of Vaishno Devi along with Ganesha, Radha-Krishna, Hanuman, Kali and Shiva. Per visitor accounts, the site originally held a ~100-year-old Maa Dakshineshwari Kali temple established by a Paramhans — said to be the origin of the locality's name 'Kalibari' — whose samadhi lies in the Kali shrine; the temple was later rebuilt and dedicated to Maa Vaishno Devi (oral tradition; UNVERIFIED by authoritative sources). MEDIA EMPTY: no reliable image of this specific temple found after genuine searching — do not substitute the Gannipur Vaishno Devi temple photos.

name: Maa Vaishno Devi Mandir
town_description: Muzaffarpur is a major city of north Bihar and the headquarters of Muzaffarpur district in the Tirhut division, famous across India for its Shahi litchis. Situated on the Burhi Gandak river, it is an important commercial hub and railway junction of the region. The city also has historical associations with Jubba Sahni and the freedom fighter Khudiram Bose, and hosts Bihar's only planetarium and the L. S. College campus.
